small_guidance:
- The compile failure is because `compute_group_stats_kernel` is not autotuned and doesn't receive `BLOCK_S` — pass `BLOCK_S=256` (or similar) explicitly as a kwarg at launch, or wrap it in `@triton.autotune`. Also pass `eps` as a Python float constexpr (not positional) to avoid launcher specialization issues.
- Add an `@triton.autotune` decorator on the stats kernel with configs over `BLOCK_S` ∈ {256,512,1024} and `num_warps` ∈ {4,8}; key on `['C','S']`.
- In the LSE kernel, hoist the `mean/invstd/gamma/beta` loads out of the channel loop by pre-broadcasting per-group scalars; consider tiling channels with `BLOCK_C` to enable register reuse.
large_guidance:
- The torch `nn.Conv2d` is still the dominant cost (8→64 channels, 3×3, 128×128, batch 128). Replacing the conv with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM (one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), implicit im2col gather) is the highest-headroom move. Fuse bias into the epilogue.
- Better still: fuse the conv epilogue with the GroupNorm stats path. Since GN needs per-(N, group) sum and sum-of-squares, have the conv kernel atomically accumulate partial sums into a `[N, GROUPS]` buffer as it produces outputs, eliminating a separate stats pass — or write conv output to memory once and run a single fused stats+LSE kernel that reads it twice from L2.
- Alternative single-pass design: after a custom conv, use one persistent kernel per (N, spatial-tile) that loads the full channel column into registers/SMEM once, computes per-group mean/invstd inline, then applies tanh/hardswish/residual/LSE — eliminating the intermediate `mean`/`invstd` global buffers and the second full read of `x_conv`.
